=== WHAT I DID ===

Re-mechanized the B1 lemma tests in src/rules.zig so the falsified old wording can never pass silently again (the G5 debt, T384). Four jobs, all done.

1. NEW 3×3 corrected-predicate test (exhaustive): enumerates every legal P₀ (no dead stones) and every two-ply capture–recapture window P₀ →(W captures 1)→ P₁ →(B captures 1)→ P₂, then checks the corrected predicate — the set of White moves from P₂ that recreate P₁ is exactly {ko point} iff the shape rule set a ko point. Reproduced T380 F-3 exactly: checked=784, ban_mismatches=0 (0 violations).

2. NEW negative control (old wording): the same census computes the OLD predicate's mismatch count (P₂ == P₀ ⇔ shape rule fires) and asserts it equals 152/784 (checked=784, window_mismatches=152). If a refactor ever makes the old wording pass, this arm goes red — the falsification stays load-bearing instead of prose.

3. Lemma text fixed: the comment block at the top of the lemma section now states the corrected wording (shape rule fires ⇔ the recapture it bans recreates P₁, the position one state back), cites T380 F-3 and T384, and the 2×2/3×2 tests are re-scoped to 'OLD window predicate holds at this size' — they no longer read as tests of the general lemma.

4. Controls before the reading counts. (a) Seeded-defect control: dropped the friendly-neighbour clause in koAfterCapture ('liberties == 1 and friendly == 0' → 'liberties == 1'). The new 3×3 corrected-predicate arm went RED: ban_mismatches 0 → 56, and the negative control's window_mismatches shifted 152 → 208 (also red on its own assertion). The existing koAfterCapture agreement tests also went red (2×2 0→8, 3×2 0→70, 3×3 sample), as expected. Reverted → all 80 tests green. (b) The existing seeded-mutant arm ('Z-R-MOVE-B1-EQUIV: seeded mutant — broken ko rule fails lemma') still exercises the same friendly-neighbour clause (its mutant flips friendly==0 to friendly!=0 and must disagree with the real kernel); it passes in the green run, confirming the touched path is covered.

=== UNEXPECTED FINDING (defect found in something I was not working on) ===

The existing `hasDeadStones` legality filter was per-stone, not per-chain: it flagged any stone with no EMPTY neighbour as 'dead', which over-filters multi-stone chains (a stone in the middle of a living group has no empty neighbour but its chain has a liberty). Following the brief's instruction to reuse it verbatim reproduced only 432 checked windows at 3×3, not T380's 784. I rewrote it as a chain-flood (same as Enumerator.is_legal / exp6.genericIsLegal) and the census then reproduced 784/152/0 exactly. This means the old 2×2/3×2 lemma tests were under-testing too (e.g. 3×2 now checks 12 windows; the old count is unrecorded but smaller). The fix is committed in the same file; the 2×2 test remains vacuous (checked==0, comment accurate).

The red-then-green cycle was real but the red exposed a latent defect rather than a pre-planned failing assertion.

=== COMMIT-PATH NOTE (tooling observation) ===
`tools/git-commit-mine` refused `src/rules.zig` because T573's `bundle` field in `docs/infra/managent/tasks.json` is stored as an ABSOLUTE path (`/Users/alex/Project/Zig/weizigo/untracked/T573-...`), while the wrapper's scope resolution concatenates `$REPO/$bundle_path` (expecting repo-relative, as every other task stores). The absolute+relative concatenation yields a non-existent path, so `deliverables=` never resolves and the scope check drops the declared engine file. Committed via `--explicit` (the documented loud escape) naming exactly the three files. The data fix (store the bundle repo-relative) is the Orchestrator's/kanban's, not this row's.
